venue.name: Nanaimo Art Gallery
venue.description: Nanaimo Art Gallery is a public contemporary art gallery at 150 Commercial Street in downtown Nanaimo, with an adjoining space called Art Lab. Admission is by donation with a suggested donation of $5, and it is open Tuesday to Saturday 10am to 5pm and Sunday noon to 5pm. Four exhibitions run each year, and the gallery offers guided group tours of the current exhibition, guided school tours with a hands on art activity, and an Artists in the Schools program that sends practising artists into classrooms in SD68 and SD69. It also runs Saturday art classes and summer camps that families register for one child at a time.

facility_notes.washrooms: A single room, gender neutral washroom is available both inside the Gallery and inside Art Lab. The counter tops in each washroom are 32" high. Change tables are available in both washrooms.
facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Street-level access is located via our front entrance on Commercial Street. There are two sets of double automated doors to pass through before entering the Gallery.
facility_notes.bus_parking: There is no public parking lot for Gallery visitors. Paid street parking is available. The nearest parkade is on the corner of Bastion & Fitzwilliam Streets behind the Royal Bank.

venue.hours_notes: Tuesday to Saturday 10am to 5pm, Sunday 12pm to 5pm. Admission is by donation, with a suggested donation of $5 and free admission for those who identify as Indigenous.

programs.name: Exhibition Tour
programs.description: A 45 minute guided tour of the gallery's current exhibition led by a gallery facilitator. The $75 covers the first 15 people and every person after that is $5. Four exhibitions run each year, so the tour changes with what is on the walls. French tours are available on request, depending on staff being available. The tours page does not give an age range for this one.
programs.what_children_do: Walk through the gallery with a facilitator, stop in front of the works in the current exhibition, and talk about what they are looking at.
programs.our_note: It is 45 minutes of standing and looking, so it works best with a group already comfortable being indoors and reasonably quiet. Folding stools are kept at the desk for anyone who needs to sit, so ask at the front when you arrive rather than partway through.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms with change tables are inside both the gallery and Art Lab, and the route in is step free with automated doors. There is no lunch space mentioned and no parking lot of their own, so plan for street parking or the parkade and eat elsewhere.
programs.evidence: Bring your group for a tour of our current exhibition led by a gallery facilitator. $5/person after the first 15 participants. $75 45 min

programs.name: Exhibition Tour and Workshop
programs.description: A 90 minute visit that pairs the guided exhibition tour with an art activity based on the themes of the show. The $200 covers the first 15 people and every person after that is $15. French tours are available on request, depending on staff being available. The tours page does not give an age range for this one.
programs.what_children_do: Tour the current exhibition with a facilitator, then sit down and make something of their own in an art activity built around the same ideas.
programs.our_note: The making half is what carries younger groups through, so this is the better of the two tours if your children will not last 45 minutes on their feet just looking. Ask what the activity involves before you come, because it changes with each exhibition.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms with change tables are inside both the gallery and Art Lab, and the route in is step free. No lunch space is mentioned and there is no parking lot of their own, so plan street parking or the parkade.
programs.evidence: art activity related to the themes in our current exhibition. $15/person after the first 15 participants. $200 90 min

programs.name: Gallery school tour
programs.description: A guided interactive tour of the current exhibition for a school class, followed by a hands on art activity inspired by it. The gallery's own workshop directory lists it as School Tour and Activity for kindergarten to grade 12. Visits run 1.5 hours, Tuesday to Friday, and can be paired with a visit to Nanaimo Museum and lunch at the Harbourfront library so two classes share one bus. With four exhibitions a year, classes are invited to come back for a different visit. No price is published for this one.
programs.what_children_do: Look at and talk about the works in the current exhibition with a gallery facilitator, then make their own piece in an art activity based on the show.
programs.our_note: Nothing on their schools pages tells you what this costs, and the group price on their tours page may or may not be the same thing, so get the number in writing before you commit a class budget. If you are coming from out of town, ask about pairing it with the museum and the library so one bus covers two stops.
programs.practical_summary: Washrooms with change tables are inside both the gallery and Art Lab, and the way in is step free with automated doors. There is no lunch room at the gallery and no parking lot of their own, so sort out lunch and the bus before you come.
programs.cancellation_note: Cancellations - we require one week's written notice to cancel a school Program at no charge. An administration fee of $20 will be charged if insufficient notice is given.
programs.evidence: Gallery and Museum visits are each 1.5 hours in length, and available Tuesday through Friday.

programs.name: Artists in the Schools
programs.description: The gallery sends practising artists into classrooms in SD68 and SD69 to run hands on workshops. The directory on their schools page lists 21 of them, in visual art, pottery, dance, theatre, music and creative writing, each with its own grade band and its own artist. Titles include Clay Story Stones, Pinch Pot Creatures, Drama Games Galore, Styrofoam Plate Printing and Zine Making, and the bands run from kindergarten to grade 12. Bookings are taken through the school year, at least two weeks ahead, and the form also accepts schools and organisations in Nanaimo, Ladysmith, Parksville and Qualicum. No price is published.
programs.what_children_do: Work with a visiting artist in their own classroom, making something with their hands or performing, depending on which workshop the teacher picks.
programs.our_note: This is the one that comes to you, which saves the bus entirely. Pick the workshop first, because each one has its own grade band and its own artist with their own free weekdays, and then give the gallery three possible dates as they ask.
programs.practical_summary: It happens in your room, so washrooms, lunch and parking are your own. What is missing is the price, which is nowhere on the site, and the form asks for a contact for invoicing, so there is a charge to ask about.
programs.cancellation_note: Cancellations - we require one week's written notice to cancel a school Program at no charge. An administration fee of $20 will be charged if insufficient notice is given.
programs.evidence: Artists in the Schools brings practicing artists into classrooms across SD68 and SD69 to lead hands-on workshops in a variety of disciplines

gaps: Price for a school visit: not published. The schools page describes a 90 minute gallery school tour with a hands on activity but never gives a figure, and the tours page prices a 90 minute tour with an art activity at $200 for a group. The site never says whether those are the same thing, so we have not put a price on the school tour. Ask for the school rate in writing.
Price for Artists in the Schools: not published. The booking form asks for a school contact for invoicing, so there is a charge, but no amount appears anywhere on the site.

Youngest age: the school offerings are written in grades from kindergarten up, and the group tours on the tours page carry no age range at all. Nothing on the site addresses under fives, so we have not answered whether daycare groups are hosted.
How many adults have to come: not published. No ratio, no free chaperone count and no adult price for any group tour.
Capacity: no maximum group size is published. The tour prices cover the first 15 people and charge per person after that, but that is a price break, not a limit.

Lunch space: not published. The schools page suggests meeting at the Vancouver Island Regional Library's Harbourfront branch for lunch when you pair a visit with Nanaimo Museum, which suggests there is nowhere to eat at the gallery, but it does not say so.
Rain backup: not addressed, although the whole visit takes place indoors.
Bus parking: not addressed. The site says there is no public parking lot for gallery visitors and points to paid street parking and a parkade behind the Royal Bank on Bastion and Fitzwilliam.
Booking email: the gallery hides its email addresses behind Cloudflare protection, so we could not read one. Use the school booking form or the phone number.
Start times: no time slots are published. School visits are Tuesday to Friday and the gallery opens at 10am.

RETRIEVAL NOTE: the address in our list, www.nanaimogallery.ca, no longer works. The www host returns a Cloudways 403 in a browser, and a plain fetch of it returns a cached copy of the gallery's 2019 website with 2019 exhibition dates and a different address for the gallery. The bare domain nanaimogallery.ca redirects to the live site at nanaimoartgallery.ca, which is what we used. A fetch only re-run against the www address will quietly produce a record that is seven years out of date.

The list of 21 Artists in the Schools workshops, with their grade bands, disciplines and artists, only appears when the page runs its scripts. A plain fetch of the schools page returns the surrounding text and an empty template where the list should be.
The gallery's social sharing image is its logo rather than a photograph, so the hero here is the lead photograph from the visit page instead.
The map on the visit page is only scrolled to a wide view of the Nanaimo area, about 10km from the gallery, so the coordinates here come from the street address instead.
